headline: SILVER AND GOLD ENTER CRITICAL WEEK: FOMC MINUTES AUG 19 + JACKSON HOLE AUG 28 — TWIN CATALYSTS SET Q4 DIRECTION
snippet: Gold entered the week of August 18 at $4,377 per ounce — recovering from Friday's pullback to $4,365 — as the two most important macro events of the month arrive in rapid succession. On Wednesday August 19, the Federal Reserve publishes minutes from its July 28-29 FOMC meeting — the first detailed window into how the Committee is splitting on the September rate decision — and on Friday August 28, Fed Chair Kevin Warsh delivers his debut Jackson Hole keynote, widely framed as the equivalent of a new central banker's inaugural policy address. The prior meeting was decided by the narrowest margin in recent memory: nine members favoured an additional rate hike versus eight voting to pause, a 9-to-8 split that has gold consolidating in the $4,350–$4,414 range as traders price approximately 60% probability of one further hike before year-end. Silver at $65.33 is broadly flat on the week. Gold fell approximately $80 in the three days after the July 14 FOMC minutes were published before recovering; the current technical base — four months of consolidation between $4,350 and $4,500 — is better established than the positioning ahead of that release. For precious metals investors, the setup is binary: dovish minutes shift momentum back toward $4,500-plus; a hawkish-majority revelation tests $4,200-$4,250 before Jackson Hole provides the reset. The Iran war premium continues to provide a geopolitical floor estimated at $150-$200 per ounce, insensitive to rate-hike probability — meaning even a hawkish FOMC minutes print faces a structural bid that did not exist in prior cycles. Warsh's August 28 keynote remains the event with the single largest potential gold price move.

headline: TOP 50 MINERS ADD $206B IN 7 SESSIONS AS GOLD TOPS $4,500 — NEWMONT +$22.5B, AGNICO +$17.9B IN A FORTNIGHT
snippet: The combined market capitalisation of the world's 50 largest mining companies rose by $206 billion in just seven trading sessions during the first two weeks of August 2026, according to IndexBox and MINING.COM data, as gold prices briefly topped $4,500 per ounce — their highest level since late March. Of the total gain, $108 billion accrued to gold, silver, and royalty companies specifically, making precious metals equity investors the primary beneficiaries of the August move. Newmont Corporation added $22.5 billion in market value over the fortnight and Agnico Eagle contributed $17.9 billion, together accounting for roughly 40% of the gold sector's total gain. Despite the headline figures, a crucial performance divergence undercuts the sector narrative: copper and diversified mining companies have added $246 billion year-to-date (+24%), while gold, silver, and royalty companies have added only $18 billion year-to-date (+2.6%). Eight of the eighteen precious metals companies in the top-50 ranking are still down on the year — including Barrick (-6.7%), Gold Fields (-8.8%), Fresnillo (-9.5%), and Shandong Gold (-19.9%). The sector's combined $2.375 trillion market cap remains approximately one-tenth the size of the Magnificent 7 technology bloc at $23.4 trillion. For retail investors, the gap between gold's 66% year-to-date price gain and mining equities' collective 2.6% market cap gain — while beginning to close — implies that mid-tier and junior gold producer re-ratings may still be in early innings, with the most significant equity upside yet to crystallise relative to the magnitude of the underlying commodity move.

headline: ARIZONA GOLD & SILVER (TSX-V: AZS) DRILLS 21.79m AT 4.10 g/t GOLD — PERRY ZONE EXTENDS 150m VERTICALLY WITH EXPANDED BLM PERMIT
snippet: Arizona Gold & Silver Inc. (TSX-V: AZS, OTCQB: AZASF) reported August 13 that drill hole PC26-169 at its 100%-owned Philadelphia Project in southern Arizona returned 21.79 metres grading 4.10 g/t gold and 5.8 g/t silver within a broader mineralised interval of 73.46 metres at 1.69 g/t gold — extending high-grade gold mineralisation approximately 150 metres vertically above previously reported Perry Zone intersections. Hole PC26-167 added 15.24 metres at 2.66 g/t gold and 5.6 g/t silver within a 66.81-metre outer envelope at 1.12 g/t gold. The deep anchor for the program is a previously confirmed interval of 9.04 g/t gold and 34 g/t silver over 20.43 metres at 320.73 metres depth — results to date confirm the Perry Zone extends both laterally and down-dip from that high-grade core. Crucially, the company has received an expanded US Bureau of Land Management permit providing access to 16 additional drill pads, enabling systematic testing of the Perry Zone's projected down-dip continuation beneath the hematite and argillic alteration cap that defines the known resource boundary above. Arizona epithermal gold-silver systems with this geometry — broad low-grade haloes enclosing high-grade internal veins extending at least 320 metres depth — have historically supported 1-3 million ounce resource estimates in the Basin and Range province. The combination of expanding geometry, confirmed depth continuity, and a new BLM permit covering fresh ground makes the next batch of drill results potentially resource-defining rather than merely confirmatory. At $4,400 gold, the economic threshold for an Arizona-jurisdiction gold resource is the lowest it has been in the history of the district.

headline: OREZONE GOLD (TSX: ORE) Q2: 58,566 OZ IN FIRST FULL MULTI-MINE QUARTER — $119.6M EBITDA AT $4,588 AVG REALISED PRICE
snippet: Orezone Gold Corporation (TSX: ORE) delivered Q2 2026 results on August 12 marking the first complete quarter of multi-mine operations following the acquisition of Casa Berardi in Quebec from Hecla Mining earlier in 2026. The company produced 58,566 gold ounces across two operating assets — Bomboré in Burkina Faso contributed 38,063 ounces (processing 2.48 million tonnes at 0.55 g/t) while the newly integrated Casa Berardi mine in Quebec added 20,503 ounces. First-half 2026 production totalled 97,355 ounces at an average realised price of US$4,588 per ounce sold. Q2 EBITDA reached $119.6 million and adjusted EBITDA $134.4 million; H1 totals were $211 million and $228.7 million respectively. Management highlighted Bomboré's resource expansion potential ahead of a mineral resource estimate update, with the open-pit geometry in Burkina Faso representing meaningful additional ounce upside pending the update. For investors evaluating mid-tier gold producers, Orezone's Q2 illustrates the financial mechanics of acquisition-driven production growth in a record-margin environment: adding Casa Berardi expanded annualised production by roughly 55% while fixed corporate overhead was essentially unchanged, compressing cost-per-ounce ratios across the consolidated operation. The $4,588 average realised price — above the August 12 spot price at the time of reporting — reflects the favourable market structure during Q2 and warrants monitoring in Q3 guidance for any hedging or streaming arrangements that could constrain participation in further spot price gains. Orezone remains one of a small number of TSX-listed gold producers with two actively producing mines across different jurisdictions, providing operational diversification that single-asset peers cannot offer.

headline: BLACKROCK AND JPMORGAN: SILVER HITS $80 BY YEAR-END 2026 AND $100 BY 2030 AS SIX-YEAR SUPPLY DEFICIT COMPOUNDS
snippet: BlackRock and J.P. Morgan Research analysts have each independently published August 2026 forecasts projecting silver will surpass $80 per ounce before December 31, 2026 — a 22% gain from current levels near $65 — with longer-term targets of $100 per ounce by 2030. J.P. Morgan's formal base case calls for silver to average $70 per ounce for full-year 2026 and normalise the gold-to-silver ratio toward 65:1 in H2 — which at $4,400 gold implies approximately $67.7 silver, confirming the market is already approaching the conservative target. Their bullish scenario, incorporating continued geopolitical uncertainty and accelerating industrial demand, projects prices testing historical highs. The structural foundation of both forecasts is the same: the Silver Institute projects 2026 will record the sixth consecutive annual supply deficit, with global mine output unable to keep pace with demand from solar panels (232 million ounces consumed in 2025, a new record), AI data centre power infrastructure, and EV charging equipment. China's January 1, 2026 reclassification of silver as a strategic material — restricting export licences to 44 approved companies — has added an additional geopolitical dimension to the structural supply constraint. For retail investors calibrating position sizing: the BlackRock and JPMorgan $80 year-end target represents the conservative institutional case. The arithmetic of the gold-to-silver ratio provides context: at the 2011 gold bull market peak ratio of 32:1 and today's gold price, silver would trade at approximately $137 per ounce. The structural drivers both firms cite are present-tense fundamentals, not forward-looking assumptions.

headline: EV BATTERY METALS INDEX HITS 27-MONTH HIGH — COBALT DOUBLES TO $25+, LITHIUM DOUBLES FROM 2025 LOWS, NICKEL REBOUNDS
snippet: The composite EV battery metals index tracked by MINING.COM reached its highest level since May 2024 in August 2026, with all four constituent metals — lithium, cobalt, nickel, and manganese — advancing simultaneously for the first time in over two years. Cobalt recovered from a 2025 trough near $10 per pound to above $25 per pound, driven by combined supply disruptions in the Democratic Republic of Congo including artisanal mining crackdowns, processing delays, and the August 6 export ban on copper and cobalt concentrates. Analysts at Credendo project cobalt will remain in a $24-$29 per pound range through year-end given tight DRC supply and persistently low circulating inventory. Lithium spot prices have more than doubled from 2025 lows and are trading above $20 per kilogram — the economic viability threshold for most hard-rock spodumene projects — with Mineral Resources, Core Lithium, and Sigma Lithium all announcing production resumptions in response. Nickel's recovery was catalysed by Indonesia's 2026 ore production quota reduction, tightening a market that had been over-supplied by laterite expansion since 2021. The index reaching 27-month highs carries particular significance for exploration-stage battery metals companies on the ASX and TSX-V: institutional capital allocation to this sector typically lags commodity price recovery by 3-6 months as analysts require sustained price signals before revising project NPVs and issuing updated coverage. If the index sustains August levels into Q3, the exploration junior re-rating cycle historically associated with Phase 2 of battery metals bull runs could begin materialising in equity prices by October-November 2026.

headline: MINERAL RESOURCES BALD HILL FY27 LITHIUM GUIDANCE DUE AUGUST 27 — FIRST CONCENTRATE SHIPPED IN JULY AFTER 18-MONTH PAUSE
snippet: Mineral Resources Limited (ASX: MIN) will release FY2027 guidance for its restarted Bald Hill lithium operation on August 27, 2026 — eleven days from now — covering expected sales volumes, free-on-board costs, and capital expenditure, giving investors their first formal forward-looking framework for the recommissioned Western Australian asset. The restart is tracking on schedule: mining and crushing commenced in June following the end of an 18-month care-and-maintenance period, and first spodumene concentrate was shipped in July 2026. The Bald Hill concentrator operates at approximately 165,000 dry metric tonnes per year at 5.1% lithium oxide. Restart costs were estimated at approximately A$20 million. The 58.1 million-tonne mineral resource at 0.9% Li2O underpins a long-life operation at the current production rate. The August 27 FY27 guidance release is a discrete event risk for MinRes shareholders and for the broader lithium market: Bald Hill's realised FOB cost structure will be the first data point confirming whether Australian hard-rock spodumene restart economics work at current lithium prices (approximately $20/kg lithium carbonate equivalent). If guidance implies FOB costs below $600 per dmt of spodumene concentrate — consistent with MinRes's cost position at similar assets — the implied margin confirms that the restart economics are sound and that the company is adding sustainable production rather than burning cash at current prices. Bald Hill's August 27 disclosure coincides with the same week as Fed Chair Warsh's Jackson Hole keynote, making it a busy week for investors tracking both macro and sector-specific catalysts.

headline: KALKINE AUGUST PICKS: PAN AMERICAN SILVER AND ALAMOS GOLD LEAD MID-CAP PACK AS PRODUCERS EXTRACT RECORD MARGINS AT $4,400
snippet: Kalkine Canada's August 2026 watchlist highlights four mid-cap producers that offer distinct leverage profiles in the current $4,400 gold and $65 silver environment: Pan American Silver (TSX/NASDAQ: PAAS) is the defensive anchor, guiding 25.0-27.0 million ounces of attributable silver and 700,000-750,000 gold ounces for 2026 with multi-mine diversification across Latin America — the 2026 silver allocation alone is generating revenue at approximately three times the price prevailing when the company's cost structure was established. Alamos Gold (TSX: AGI) offers pure Canadian production leverage through its Island Gold mine in Ontario, where the Phase 3 expansion underway targets 287,000 ounces per year at operating costs among the lowest in Canada. IAMGOLD (TSX: IMG) is the operational leverage story: Côté Gold Mine in Ontario, which reached commercial production in 2024, is generating record margins at $4,400 gold against an all-in sustaining cost below $1,200 per ounce, with the mine on track to become one of Canada's largest gold operations as throughput scales. Endeavour Mining (TSX: EDV) rounds out the set as a West Africa multi-asset producer operating across Senegal, Côte d'Ivoire, and Burkina Faso. Kalkine's thesis tracks what financial modelling confirms: at $4,400 gold, mid-cap producers with AISC below $1,500 are generating free cash flow yields of 20-30% on current enterprise values — a ratio that historically precedes sector re-ratings as institutional investors rotate out of royalty companies (high quality, lower leverage) into operating producers that offer direct earnings sensitivity to further gold price gains.

headline: GDX 108% YEAR-OVER-YEAR: GOLD MINERS ENTER RARE OUTPERFORMANCE MODE AFTER 15 YEARS TRADING AT A DISCOUNT TO BULLION
snippet: The VanEck Gold Miners ETF (GDX) has delivered a 108% total return over the past twelve months, while the VanEck Junior Gold Miners ETF (GDXJ) outperformed GDX by approximately 13 percentage points in 2025 and held that premium into 2026 — marking the first sustained period of gold equity outperformance versus physical bullion since 2011, according to analysis from Discovery Alert. The inflection point was mechanical: gold's breakthrough above $3,000 in early 2026 and subsequent advance toward $5,000 compressed mining companies' all-in sustaining costs (averaging below $2,000 per ounce) against a revenue line running $2,500-$3,500 per ounce above cost — a margin expansion that produced earnings growth at a rate no other sector could match. GDX currently trades at approximately 11.2x forward earnings, which is compelling relative to its historical range of 12x-18x in previous gold bull markets and against the S&P 500's current 21x, despite the sector posting record earnings per share. The analytical context for retail investors is the 2001-2011 comparison: during the prior gold bull market, well-selected gold mining equities returned 5-10 times the gain in physical gold. In the current cycle — gold up roughly 150% from $1,700 in January 2024 to $4,400 in August 2026 — the mining equity re-rating has returned approximately 108% year-over-year. The critical question for position-sizing decisions is whether the 11.2x P/E represents a cycle top or an early-to-middle phase of multiple expansion that historically requires gold prices to plateau at elevated levels for 12-24 months before the full earnings re-rating completes.

headline: GOLD M&A TOPS $7.9B IN 2026 — BUT THE NEW PROBLEM IS A SHRINKING PIPELINE OF JUNIOR DEVELOPERS READY FOR ACQUISITION
snippet: Gold sector M&A has exceeded $7.9 billion in announced transaction value through August 2026 — a pace that tracks well above the prior three-year average — with major completed deals including Equinox Gold's $5.1 billion acquisition of Orla Mining (completed August 3), the $1.95 billion Barrick-Newmont Nevada Gold Mines restructuring, and the abandoned $3.9 billion Zijin Mining approach to Allied Gold. Yet analysts at Crux Investor have identified a structural constraint that could slow the pace: the pipeline of acquisition-ready junior developers is thinner than any prior gold M&A cycle in the past 25 years. The root cause is a decade of exploration underinvestment. Exploration-stage junior companies that would typically be advancing toward production decisions in a $4,400 gold environment were largely unfunded through the 2016-2023 period when gold remained below $2,500 and exploration capital fled to technology and energy transition sectors. The practical consequence: senior producers seeking to replace depleting reserves are being forced to either acquire projects at earlier development stages (accepting additional permitting, engineering, and execution risk) or bid competitively against peers for the same limited pool of advanced assets — inflating transaction multiples in the process. For retail investors in exploration juniors, this dynamic is structurally bullish: it implies a compressed discovery-to-acquisition timeline versus historical cycles, as majors are approaching targets before traditional development milestones are reached. The geographic flip side: only projects in Tier 1 jurisdictions (Canada, Australia, USA, select West Africa) are benefiting. Projects in higher-risk jurisdictions face a higher acquisition premium hurdle that may not be cleared regardless of gold's price.

headline: THE FED IS SPLIT 9-TO-8: WHAT WEDNESDAY'S FOMC MINUTES MEAN FOR GOLD — AND WHY JACKSON HOLE IS THE BIGGER EVENT
snippet: The Federal Reserve's July 28-29 FOMC meeting concluded with the narrowest policy vote in recent memory — nine members favouring an additional rate hike versus eight voting to pause — a split that has anchored gold in the $4,350-$4,414 consolidation range for two weeks as the market prices approximately 60% probability of one further hike. The August 19 minutes release will be the first detailed window into how each faction presented its case, revealing whether the nine hike-supporters were resolute or reluctant, and whether the eight pause-advocates are close to switching sides on further economic data. Gold's historical reaction to FOMC minutes in the current cycle is informative: the July 14 release — which revealed a similar split at the prior meeting — produced an approximately $80 per ounce decline in the three trading days following publication, before the Iran war premium reasserted as the dominant driver. The structural difference entering August 19 is that four months of consolidation between $4,350 and $4,500 has built a more robust technical base, meaning the same hawkish minutes impulse would likely produce a smaller and shorter correction from a technically stronger platform. The more important event for gold direction remains the August 28 Jackson Hole keynote from Fed Chair Kevin Warsh — it is his first major address as Fed Chair and will be treated as a policy signal regardless of its formal framing. GoldSilver.com's analysis argues that Warsh's framing of the inflation-versus-growth trade-off will set gold's Q4 range more definitively than any individual data release, making August 28 the event that actually matters for positioning heading into year-end.

headline: GOLD STOCKS MAY STILL OUTPERFORM GOLD IN 2026 — VALUATIONS 14% BELOW FEB PEAK DESPITE RECORD MARGINS ACROSS THE SECTOR
snippet: Despite GDX delivering 108% year-over-year returns and the sector recording an August week in which $108 billion of market cap was added across gold and silver companies, the combined sector valuation remains approximately 14% below its February 2026 peak — when the top 50 mining companies reached $2,748 billion before gold's pullback from the January high of $5,600 per ounce. The sector's current valuation relative to commodity prices remains lower than before last year's major rally, and if gold prices remain at current levels or continue rising, current share prices do not yet fully reflect those higher price assumptions. Eight of the top eighteen precious metals companies in the global ranking are still down year-to-date including major names like Barrick Gold (-6.7%), Gold Fields (-8.8%), and Fresnillo (-9.5%) — creating a valuation dispersion that looks anomalous in a $4,400 gold environment. The analytical case for gold equity outperformance versus bullion through the end of 2026 rests on three converging factors: compressed valuations relative to record earnings, a $108 billion sector market cap gain in one fortnight demonstrating rapid institutional capital rotation back into the sector, and the approaching FOMC/Jackson Hole events that could remove the interest-rate uncertainty that has capped equity multiples even as physical gold advanced. For retail investors using GDX or GDXJ as a proxy for leverage to gold prices, the 14% sector-wide discount to the February peak — at a gold price only marginally below February levels — represents exactly the kind of asymmetric setup that has historically preceded the next leg of miner outperformance in extended gold bull markets.
